title: This Nebula Looks Like a Shark - Nautilus
gist: Lynds Dark Nebula 1235, a shark-shaped cloud of gas and dust about 15 light-years long first spotted in the 1960s, returned to attention via Ali Alobaidly's photo that won first prize in the Royal Observatory Greenwich's ZWO Astronomy Photographer of the Year competition.

insights.claim: Lynds Dark Nebula 1235, the 'shark' nebula, is a silhouette of interstellar gas and dust stretching about 15 light-years from head to tail, roughly four times the Sun-Proxima Centauri distance.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Pure science-interest item with no direct market implications.

insights.claim: Lynds Dark Nebula 1235 was first spotted in the 1960s but has returned to public attention thanks to a new photograph.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Shows how competitions and imagery, not new science, drive public attention to astronomy.

insights.claim: Photographer Ali Alobaidly's image of the shark nebula won first prize in the Royal Observatory Greenwich's ZWO Astronomy Photographer of the Year competition, with judges calling it 'perfectly rendered' and at the forefront of modern-day astrophotography.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Amateur astrophotography quality is reaching a level judges deem cutting-edge, reflecting improving consumer imaging equipment.
insights.quote: at the very forefront of modern-day astrophotography
